lines: High-yield bond pioneer Mike Milken argues access to capital is the key multiplier for human and social capital, which he values at six to seven times all global financial assets combined.

He says non-investment-grade companies were the main job engine of the late 20th century, creating over 60 million jobs while investment-grade firms shed a net 4 million, and fueled industries like cable, telecom and biotech.

Milken contends risk is widely misunderstood: lower-quality debt has often delivered better risk-adjusted returns because premiums are mispriced, sovereign debt is not as safe as assumed, and the real systemic danger is maturity mismatch between short-term liabilities and long-term assets.
He credits healthcare and public-health advances with more than half of global economic growth over the past century, adding over 40 years to life expectancy, as the case for long-term investment.

He links public distrust of finance to fewer professionals wanting to 'change the world' (from about 25% in the 1970s to 1% today), and reads the migration of wealthy entrepreneurs as a leading indicator of future job hubs.
podcast: In Good Company with Nicolai Tangen
title: Mike Milken: Access to Capital, the American Dream, and Why Risk Is Misunderstood
